#1890. Liverpool suspension risks: Key star walking Premier League tightrope before Manchester United clash

Liverpool are in a good place as the season pauses for the final international break of the year.

Andoni Iraola's side bounced back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce to beat Crystal Palace at the weekend, a result that has lifted them into the top-four of the Premier League table.

The Reds have also picked up nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase of this season's Champions League, leaving them in a great position to qualify for the round of 16 stage.

Furthermore, a place in the Carabao Cup semi-final beckons should they overcome Iraola's former club Bournemouth at Anfield before Christmas.

For now though, the Spaniard will be hopeful that all of his international stars return from duty unscathed as a huge game greets Liverpool upon their return to Premier League action - the visit of Manchester United.

While United have been disappointing in the league this season, sitting in the relegation zone after failing to beat Aston Villa, the Reds were beaten in the corresponding fixture just over a year ago when Harry Maguire stunned Anfield with a late winner.

It remains to be seen if Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong will recover from injury to be available for selection against Man Utd, but one key Liverpool player will have to be careful if selected due to the looming threat of a ban.

With that in mind, here’s a look at the Liverpool players at risk of suspension.

As every club have already been made fully aware of this season, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Liverpool's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Coventry on January 2, 2027.

From that point onwards, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Alexis Mac Allister is the big suspension concern for Liverpool at present. After being booked in the win over Crystal Palace, the Argentina international is only one yellow card away from a ban so must watch his step against United.

If booked against Man Utd, Mac Allister would be banned for the first Merseyside derby of the season away at Everton the following week.

Ultimately, the midfielder is walking the disciplinary tightrope for games against Man United, Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham, Hull, Aston Villa and Coventry.

Ronald Araujo, Bradley Barcola, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk are on three yellow cards, while Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz are among a host of Liverpool players still in danger of being suspended.

Three yellow cards: Ronald Araujo, Bradley Barcola, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk

Two yellow cards: Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz

#1889. Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Pascal Gross equals Mesut Ozil Premier League record

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:16, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 16:31

Brighton & Hove Albion playmaker Pascal Gross equalled a Premier League record set by Mesut Ozil in the Seagulls' 2-0 triumph over Brentford on Sunday afternoon.

Fabian Hurzeler's men enhanced their Premier League title credentials once again at the Amex Stadium, where first-half goals from Gross and Diego Gomez either side of Igor Thiago's red card did the damage.

After Gomez propelled Brighton into the ascendancy with just 15 minutes gone, Gross was given the chance to double the Seagulls' lead from the penalty spot thanks to Keane Lewis-Potter's challenge on Luka Vuskovic.

The veteran midfielder made no mistake with an incredible top-corner strike to rubber-stamp Brighton's victory, and in turn equal Ozil's record for the most combined Premier League goals and assists from a German player.

Gross has now had a direct hand 87 Premier League goals - 35 of his own and 52 assists - while Ozil managed 33 goals and 54 assists during his time in the top flight with Arsenal.

87 - Pascal Groß and Mesut Özil are now tied for the most goal involvements by ?? German players in the Premier League: Özil - 33 goals, 54 assists Groß - 35 goals, 52 assists Playmakers. https://t.co/hQxnGBczxO

The 35-year-old Gross has also had a direct hand in 10 goals in as many Premier League matches in the 2026-27 season, scoring four of his own while setting up six more for the Seagulls.

Already a fan favourite during his first stint at the Amex Stadium, Gross has been nothing short of a revelation for the Seagulls since returning from Borussia Dortmund in 2025 for a second stint on the South Coast.

Also now just one game away from reaching 300 in a Brighton kit, Gross will almost certainly break Ozil's record before the season is over, although he has a bit further to go to become the highest scoring German in Premier League history.

That record was broken just last week, as Arsenal's Kai Havertz scored his 46th Premier League goal against Liverpool, surpassing Ilkay Gundogan's previous best of 45 for Premier League Germans.

Nevertheless, Gross's 35 puts him third in the charts, while his next active closest challenger is Brentford's Kevin Schade, who has netted 24 goals in the English top flight.

Beating Arsenal at home, Manchester City away and slaying aside almost every other foe in their path, Brighton could do little more to cement their status as serious Premier League title challengers.

The Seagulls have now risen to second place in the Premier League table behind Arsenal, sitting five points adrift of the reigning champions and one clear of a struggling Manchester City side.

Furthermore, the Citizens' place in the top flight remains in major doubt as fans await the verdict of their appeal against 114 charges, while Liverpool and Chelsea have lacked consistency since the campaign began.

The sample size remains small, but after 10 matches, Brighton have shown every sign of lasting the course and pushing the holders all the way.

#1888. Diego Simeone ‘dreaming’ of January transfer move for £60m Arsenal star

Atletico Madrid are plotting an ambitious January transfer move for out-of-favour Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi helped bring Arsenal’s painful 22-year wait for a Premier League title to an end last season, making 34 starts across the top-flight campaign while racking up five goals and an assist.

The 27-year-old was also instrumental in the Champions League as the Gunners progressed to the final for just the second time in the club’s history, only to lose on penalties to PSG in the final.

However, a combination of injury problems, Myles Lewis-Skelly’s resurgence in central midfield and the high-profile summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes have seen Zubimendi slide down the pecking order in north London.

All seven of Zubimendi’s league appearances this season have come from the substitutes bench and the Spain international has grown frustrated with his peripheral role under Mikel Arteta, desperate for more minutes.

According to Spanish radio station RNE via SPORT, Atletico Madrid have been alerted to the situation as they scour the market for possible midfield reinforcements.

It’s claimed Atleti’s sporting director, Mateu Alemany, believes there is major room for improvement within Diego Simeone’s squad despite the club investing heavily in new recruits in the summer.

Zubimendi’s name is said to have ’emerged as a potential target’ and the 2026 World Cup winner could be ‘one of the prized signings’ of the January transfer window if his struggles continue at Arsenal.

Atleti chiefs are realistic that successfully pulling off such an operation would ‘not be easy’ and are aware that they are not alone in eyeing a move for Zubimendi, with fierce rivals Real Madrid known to be admirers.

The Spaniard has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract at the Emirates.

‘But his energy, his application and his will to help are unquestionable, and he’s an unbelievable player for us.’

#1885. Why Enzo Maresca is sticking with 'awe-inspiring' Gianluigi Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show, growing catalogue of errors and a worrying downward trend

Published: 12:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 07:07 EST, 6 November 2026

There was a Manchester City fan on Thursday’s Ryanair flight back home from Leipzig wearing a Gianluigi Donnarumma sticker on his coat, portraying the Italian as Don Vito Corleone. The sticker, a bit worn and a bit crumpled, was peeling off. A metaphor exists within that somewhere.

Tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League – beaten at his near post by Ridle Baku's cross for one goal, fumbling another routine effort at the feet of a striker and allowing a straightforward shot to squirm through his fingers – just adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Question marks around Donnarumma’s suitability between the sticks are becoming more pronounced after a catalogue of mistakes this season. One against Paris Saint-Germain when Maghnes Akliouche’s shot was too hot (some would argue two after neglecting his near post for Desire Doue’s opener) and then Nicolas Jackson shooting through him at Aston Villa last month.

Each time, Enzo Maresca has publicly recognised the errors and intimated that nobody needs to rake over them in detail with his No1, who is experienced enough to know he must do better.

Now Leipzig. ‘It’s not a concern,’ Maresca said of the latest gaffe. The manager’s defences of Donnarumma are racking up and what City are witnessing is fundamental problems from somebody described as the best the world has to offer.

Maresca has rejected the idea that summer signing Geronimo Rulli, a 34-year-old Argentina international, could take over the gloves, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’. Rulli understood his lot when joining from Marseille, to feature in domestic cup competitions, and was happy with that.

Gianluigi Donnarumma had a night to forget in Leipzig this week, making at least three individual errors

But Man City boss Enzo Maresca will stand by his goalkeeper, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’

Happy in a way that James Trafford was not, after making it clear that one season as Donnarumma’s understudy was not palatable.

He has flourished at Leeds United so far this season, leading to some observers criticising Hugo Viana for letting him go, only to blunder for a goal at Bournemouth last weekend. Worth remembering that it does happen to all of them at some point.

Trafford did not appear ready for the big time last year when starting the season ahead of the wantaway Ederson and City had their eyes on Donnarumma months before landing him – a £26million deal struck just as Ederson left for Fenerbahce.

Trafford will be ready soon and is pushing Jordan Pickford hard to be England's No1, but definitely wasn’t back then.

With Trafford gone and Maresca seemingly ruling out his No2 taking over – while also making a vague reference to taking stock over the international break – it appears that City would have no option but to stick with Donnarumma if they did actually want to bring about a change. January signings seem remote in the current climate of guilty verdicts and appeals.

But there is something outstanding that Donnarumma does offer, one that does set him apart. Maresca categorised the stunning one-handed save from Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner as one nobody else could make.

And while some hyperbole might be at play there, very few could lay claim to producing that kind of moment on a semi-regular basis.

Repelling Baumgartner is up there with Donnarumma’s instinctive save from Bryan Mbeumo at a crucial juncture on debut last year and thwarting Alexis Mac Allister in a victory at Anfield. The sort of awe-inspiring saves thousands pay money to witness.

Very few goalkeepers can claim to make wonder-saves as regularly as Donnarumma does

Donnarumma's impressive shot-stopping in the Premier League is evidenced by this graphic of every shot he has faced since joining City (red circles = goals, blank circles = saves)

Nobody across the Premier League has a higher save percentage than Donnarumma’s 71.5 since his arrival from PSG. More scientifically, only Bart Verbruggen and Senne Lammens have prevented more goals in that time – a metric measured by the xG of shots compared to how many goals were conceded.

Donnarumma has prevented seven goals (1.4 this season), with Brighton’s Verbruggen at 9.7 and Manchester United's Lammens at 8.1 across the same period. These are broadly encouraging numbers for City, despite Donnarumma's save percentage dipping to 69.7 this season – eighth among his peers, with Trafford way out in front on 79.5.

City will need to keep a careful eye on that downward trend from a 27-year-old who they brought to the club to act as the anchor, to bail them out in a way that Ederson struggled. That was the trade-off for his limited footwork, being incapable of playing through the opposition lines in a way the Brazilian could.

The wonder saves cancel all of that out. Donnarumma has been the goalkeeper’s goalkeeper for those alone. But were the certainty around that aspect of his game to waver on a longer-term basis, City should have decisions to make.

The design of AC Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season has been leaked, according to a report, featuring a black base and yellow details.

The 2027-28 season will be the last with Puma as Milan’s kit partner, as an agreement worth €50m per year has been reached with Adidas from 2028-29 onwards. It’s a switch that many fans have longed for, but right now, the focus is on whether Puma will end their tenure at the top or not.

The reality is that a lot of the Puma kits, especially the ones in recent years, have been praised by the Milan fans for their design. There’s certainly no bad blood between the parties and as such, Puma is working very hard to deliver a strong output for the last season.

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 16:17

Bristol Rovers will be looking to cause an upset when they welcome Reading to the Memorial Stadium for an EFL Trophy clash on Tuesday.

The hosts have already been eliminated from the competition, while the visitors need a convincing victory to keep their hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

Bristol Rovers currently sit 17th in League Two with 16 points from their opening 14 matches, having made a difficult start to the campaign.

However, Steve Evans's side will take encouragement from their most recent outing which saw them beat Cambridge United 2-0 in the FA Cup.

Reiss Russell-Denny and Fabrizio Cavegn were on target for Bristol Rovers as they ended a run of seven games without a win across all competitions.

The Pirates have also struggled in the EFL Trophy, collecting just one point from their opening two group fixtures after losing to Chelsea Under-21s on penalties after a 2-2 draw and suffering a 4-1 defeat to Wycombe Wanderers.

Although they are already eliminated, Bristol Rovers will be keen to build on Saturday's FA Cup victory and build some momentum ahead of their return to league action.

The Royals have also collected two points from their first two EFL Trophy fixtures, beating Wycombe on penalties after a 1-1 draw before suffering a 2-0 defeat against Chelsea Under-21s.

Reading may have to make at least one change after Udoka Godwin-Malife picked up a knock against Peterborough, with Ashqar Ahmed likely to replace him.

Marriott is also expected to be rested, having only just returned from injury, and Reid is likely to replace him after scoring his first goals for the Royals on Saturday.

#1881. Rio Ferdinand names his top choice to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Rio Ferdinand says Mauricio Pochettino is the candidate who ‘jumps off the list’ to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

Carrick, 45, looks set to be sacked following United’s disastrous start to the 2026/27 campaign.

Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break, just one point off bottom spot.

Old Trafford bosses are currently reviewing Carrick’s position but a change in the dugout appears to be the most likely outcome.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Pochettino has also emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick and Ferdinand has put his support behind the Argentine.

Pochettino, 54, signed an extension to his contract as USA coach after last summer’s World Cup but the deal is believed to contain a release clause.

‘People are talking about Mauricio Pochettino and it looks like he’s at the front of the queue right now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘We spent some time with him and his team in the summer, they’re really good guys and competent at what they do.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I look at Pochettino and one of his biggest assets is that human element of his management and building confidence with his players. That’s a big part of Manchester United at the moment because we’ve got far too many broken individuals.

‘How that gets rebuilt, is that coaching, results or somebody coming in and putting an arm around their shoulder? It’s going to be all of that.

‘I look at that group of names and think Pochettino is the one that jumps off the list as someone who has more of the things we’re looking for to save and build a group of players.

‘There’s not many names jumping off the page when you look at it. People will say, “what has Pochettino won?”, but you can say the same about Eddie Howe.

Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol before his prominence rose during a short but impressive spell in charge of Southampton.

Pochettino had mixed stints at PSG and Chelsea before taking over as coach of the United States in September 2024.

His USA team impressed in the group stages of last summer’s World Cup, topping Group D, but suffered a humbling 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last-16.

Manchester United’s first game after the international break is a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1880. Liverpool injury update: Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch, Dominik Szoboszlai latest news and return dates

Liverpool will be battling some significant fitness issues during the international break.

The two-week pause in the campaign may have not come at an ideal time for Liverpool after bouncing back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at the weekend.

Nevertheless, it’s a chance for Andoni Iraola to take stock of where his team is at and build towards a huge game at home to a Manchester United side currently in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Spaniard has made it clear that his one wish from the final international break of the year is no fresh injuries - particularly after losing Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai during the autumn window.

However, Iraola may not get his wish upon news that captain Virgil van Dijk has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad, while Szoboszlai is awaiting results of an assessment after joining up with the Hungary squad.

With that in mind, here is the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates…

The Liverpool captain was called up by new Dutch head coach Xavi for the Nations League double-header against Greece and Germany.

However, it was confirmed on Monday that he - and Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey - had pulled out of the squad for fitness related reasons.

A statement reads: “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey have been dropped from the Dutch national team's upcoming international matches. Both players did not return fit from the past weekend's matches and are therefore unavailable.

“The squad thus currently consists of 23 players.”

Liverpool fans will be hopeful this decision is no more than a precaution, particularly after Van Dijk played 90 minutes in all four Nations League games during the autumn international window.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Szoboszlai will be assessed to determine his fitness for international duty with Hungary.

The midfielder was forced off in the second half against Palace due to a knee complaint and Iraola admitted afterwards that the Reds No8 was not fully fit.

“Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” Iraola said. "Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I'm praying - it's the last thing we need.”

Liverpool dealt new fitness scare ahead of Man Utd showdown

Liverpool star in surprise international call-up after injury lay-off

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Ryan Gravenberch has missed Liverpool’s last two games with a heel injury. There was hope the Dutchman would return for the trip to Selhurst Park, but was ultimately left out of the matchday squad.

“The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” Iraola said in the pre-Crystal Palace press conference. “The others will be the same as we have been.

“The Ryan Gravenberch thing is a day-to-day thing, it’s a matter of pain. Let’s see if he can deal with the pain and he can help us.”

With the injury severe enough to prevent the midfielder from being called up by Xavi for the Netherlands’ Nations League double-header, Gravenberch must be considered a major doubt to face Man United.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Jeremie Frimpong picked up a muscle injury during the comeback win over Brentford last month, resulting in another lay-off for the full-back since his arrival from Bayer Leverkusen.

Like compatriots Van Dijk and Gravenberch, he will not be representing the Dutch during the international break and it’s believed his return is not too far away.

In the most recent update of Frimpong, Iraola said: “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Giovanno Leoni signed for Liverpool from Parma last summer in a deal worth around £26million, but a serious knee injury means he has been limited to just one senior appearance so far.

The centre-back made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September 2025, but he was stretchered off and it was later confirmed that he had suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

He was expected to miss a full year of action, which has proved to be the case.

He had hoped to have made his comeback for the recent September international break, but that has since been delayed.

“It’s taking more time than we wanted,” Iraola said. “The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

Hugo Ekitike has not played since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The Frenchman was forced to sit out the end of last season and the World Cup, where it was estimated that he would be out for nine months to a full year.

He was included in Iraola’s squad for the Champions League league phase - which came as a surprise to many - with the hope that he could potentially return for the final two games in January, against Inter Milan and Lens.

The striker is thought to be targeting a comeback before the turn of the year.

Conor Bradley is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered a serious knee injury at Arsenal back in January.

The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in that match, which has kept him out for almost a year.

Iraola’s latest comments were positive, indicating that Bradley will soon return to full training.

“[He is] doing very well,” Iraola said. “I think [he is] in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

“I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

It looks as though he could rejoin team training during the November international break.

Potential return date: Wednesday, December 2 vs Sunderland (H)

#1879. Mansfield Town vs Chesterfield - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 16:30

Mansfield Town play host to Chesterfield on Tuesday evening having already been eliminated from the EFL Trophy.

However, the visitors to Field Mill have booked their place in the knockout stages with five points from their opening two games in Group D of the Northern Section.

Nigel Clough will be disappointed with how Mansfield have fared in the EFL Trophy, losing to Manchester City Under-21s and Port Vale respectively.

Six goals have been conceded in those contests, including four versus City, but Clough will be more encouraged with their form in League One and the FA Cup.

At the weekend, Mansfield recorded a 3-0 victory over National League North high-flyers Macclesfield FC, avoiding what was viewed as a genuine cup upset possibility.

They had previously failed to beat or score versus Notts County and Wigan Athletic, yet 11 points have been accumulated from their last six matches in the third tier of English football.

That run has kept the Stags in 11th position in the League One table, just seven points adrift of second place.

In sharp contrast to Mansfield in this competition, Chesterfield have racked up five points, as well as scoring five goals versus Man City.

Paul Cook's team followed that with a penalty-shootout success over Port Vale after a 1-1 draw, and a top-two spot is now assured.

Nevertheless, Cook will have concerns over Chesterfield's recent inconsistency, with there being 18 goals in their most recent three encounters.

Although a 4-1 loss at Newport County was posted on October 30, the Spireites registered a 5-1 triumph over Crewe Alexandra in the preceding game and edged out Yeovil Town by a 4-3 scoreline in Saturday's FA Cup tie.

Clough could draft Harry Lewis, Owen Dodgson, Elliott Hewitt, Kyle Knoyle, Luke Bolton, Ollie Taylor and Tyler Roberts into his Mansfield starting lineup.

The formation that Clough will use is not obvious, a consequence of deploying different tactics for the previous two EFL Trophy games.

Deji Oshilaja is expected to remain sidelined through injury.

Meanwhile, Chesterfield youngsters Victor Huart, Gunner Elliott and Jaylen Zarb have all been called up for international duty.

Ryan Boot, Junior Eccleston, Tom Naylor, George McEachran, Dilan Markanday, Dylan Duffy, Joel Randall and Fraser Byrden are in contention for opportunities.

Boot; Hutton, Pond, Eccleston, Gordon; Naylor, McEachran; Markanday, Randell, Duffy; Bryden

While both teams will make as many changes as the EFL rule book allows, Chesterfield will be motivated to secure top spot. Therefore, even with Mansfield giving a better account of themselves in their previous group matches, we are backing the visitors to prevail by the odd goal in three.

#1878. Mauricio Pochettino has already given Manchester United an answer ahead of new manager talks

Mauricio Pochettino has previously revealed the Premier League is the “ideal place” for him to work, amid links to becoming the next Manchester United manager.

The Argentine, who managed both Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, has emerged as the new favourite to replace Michael Carrick - who is reportedly expected to be relieved of his duties as Man Utd head coach.

Following a 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United are in the relegation zone and will remain there throughout the November international break.

According to reports, Man United are anticipating a managerial change before facing bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday and Pochettino is the new leading contender, ahead of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

It is not the first time Pochettino has been linked with the Old Trafford post as it was almost a regular occurrence during his time at Tottenham.

But would he be open to a move now, should the vacancy become available in the near future? Judging by comments made in an interview with L’Equipe earlier in the year, Pochettino would be keen to manage in the Premier League again.

“I miss the football scene in England. I love the country, its culture, the football culture,” he said.

“For anyone with a competitive spirit who wants to measure themselves against others and test their limits, it's the ideal place. Here, you have to give your best constantly.”

While Pochettino misses English football, his commitments to the USMNT could prove a stumbling block if Man United do end up making an approach for the 54-year-old.

After guiding USA to a respectable round of 16 finish at the 2026 World Cup, Pochettino signed a new contract in August to stay on with the national team and his deal runs through until the 2030 World Cup.

#1877. Modric hints he could continue beyond 2026-27 season: “As long as I feel this way”

Luka Modric has hinted that he could continue playing beyond this season, having made Milan his home since arriving in 2025.

In the summer, after some speculation prior to the World Cup, Modric put pen to paper and extended his contract with Milan for another season. It was a huge boost for Ruben Amorim, who pushed for the Croatian to stay and help shape the new Milan.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A few months ago, Modric also announced that he would continue with the Croatian national team, deciding not to retire after the World Cup. It’s a pretty clear signal that he still feels in great shape and perhaps could continue beyond this season.

Speaking to this week’s edition of SportWeek, as transcribed by MilanPress, Modric shared his thoughts on the derby and the project at Milan. He also said that as long as he feels good, he will continue to play football, hinting that the 2027-28 season might not be his last.

“It was a fantastic victory and I think it was our best performance of the season. We deserved these three points, which we really needed, both for our morale and for our confidence.

“We are growing as a team, and if we can limit the dips in form that can occur over a season, we will have a chance to fight for the title, which remains our goal.

“We are putting the coach’s ideas into practice better and better, we are moving in the right direction, and our stadium is driving us: the Milan fans are incredible.”

“I feel good and I still have the passion, ambition, and strength. As long as I feel this way, I want to keep playing. I’m also loved at Milan. I had no doubts this summer, after speaking with Amorim and the club: they wanted me to stay and I just needed to feel wanted.

“Milan is my team, and I want to help the younger players develop,” he stated.

#1876. Jeglertz expects Man City consistency regardless of Champions League rotation

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andree Jeglertz wants his Manchester City players to keep imposing their own style of play upon their opponents, even if a packed schedule causes him to rotate his squad in the Champions League this week.

The English champions visit Inter on Tuesday, having thumped West Ham 5-0 last Saturday to overtake Chelsea at the top of the Women's Super League.

City then have a huge clash with Chelsea to come on Saturday, with two further games to play prior to the next international break, away to Hacken in the Champions League and at home to Tottenham in the league.

City have drawn all three of their Champions League games so far this term, with their winless run in the league stage of the competition now stretching back four games (D3 L1), after they won their previous five such matches.

Jeglertz is yet to decide how he will manage his squad over the coming days, but whoever lines up against Inter, he does not expect City's intensity to drop.

"It's only two days between these games and three days to Chelsea," Jeglertz told reporters on Monday.

"So, there are a lot of things to consider; the load for the players, how they recover from that massive game against West Ham, then how we can get the best out of the squad.

"This balance is always something to consider, but we need to figure out how we maintain our way of playing – no matter who we play, we want to play the same way.

"Okay, we play different opponents, but our identity should always be recognised, no matter if it's two days or seven days between games.

"All these games are coming in periods when you play a lot of tight and important matches in the league. The balance for us is to be able to win and get a 90-minute performance at a high level.

"That's what we aim for. There are no guarantees, but the idea and the philosophy is to perform the best we can. That's the target tomorrow, and we'll see how it goes."

#1875. Mauricio Pochettino contract clause explained as Manchester United 'learn price to appoint'

Manchester United have finally decided to sack Michael Carrick, with Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner for the Old Trafford job.

Reports emerged on Monday evening that a decision has been made to dismiss the under-pressure boss with the club in the Premier League relegation zone.

As many of the squad fly out for international duty with their respective nations, work will now begin at the club’s Carrington training ground to hire a new manager.

And former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Pochettino is the favourite.

ESPN report that Pochettino is the favoured candidate among Man Utd chiefs, but he will not come cheap.

Pochettino has not been involved in club management since his decision to leave Chelsea, by mutual contest, two and a half years ago.

The Argentine had spent just one year in west London, and was soon after lured by the USA national team to guide them into their home World Cup where they were knocked out at the last-16 stage.

Pochettino was heavily linked with a return to Tottenham before the World Cup, and was widely expected to leave the USMNT setup after the tournament.

However, in August, Pochettino signed a new contract to guide the national team into the 2030 World Cup.

But, with Man Utd now set to come calling, Pochettino is ready to head back to the Premier League.

BBC Sport report that Pochettino is open to the Old Trafford job and Man Utd will have to cough up to appoint him.

According to The Athletic, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s contract worth $10million (£7.44m) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

However, the buyout clause does not cover Pochettino’s coaching staff, many of who - such as assistant Jesus Perez - has been with him most the majority of his career.

#1874. Man United break another unwanted record vs. Aston Villa after Alysson, Nicolas Jackson goals

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:50, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 17:00

Manchester United have broken yet another unwanted club record after falling 2-0 down inside just four minutes against Aston Villa.

On the back of Tuesday's extraordinary 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League, Michael Carrick could have been forgiven for expecting a fierce response domestically on Sunday afternoon.

However, the Englishman instead oversaw yet another disastrous opening, as Villa winger Alysson took just one minute to break the deadlock with a low strike through Senne Lammens's legs.

The Red Devils then found themselves two goals behind just a few moments later, as Nicolas Jackson followed in after a Lammens save to tap home the visitors' second.

Jackson's strike marked a shocking new low for Man United, who broke their record for the quickest time to fall 2-0 down in a Premier League game at three minutes and 40 seconds.

2 - After three minutes and 40 seconds, this is the earliest Manchester United have ever been 2-0 down in a Premier League game. Slumber. https://t.co/76iMwVLhTK

Boos rang out around an already febrile Old Trafford following Jackson's goal, the ground already awash with a sea of green and yellow in protest against the Glazer family's ownership of the club.

Carrick and United's players were subsequently subjected to a collection of brutal chants from the crowd, such as "you're not fit to wear the shirt" and "you're getting sacked in the morning".

Villa fans also took aim at former midfielder Youri Tielemans, chanting "you used to play for a big club" and poking fun at Bruno Fernandes's recent public criticism, bellowing out "Bruno's right, you're f****** s****".

However, Fernandes then gave Man United a sliver of hope from the penalty spot, calmly sending Zion Suzuki the wrong way after Matheus Cunha was scythed down by Boubacar Kamara.

If the Red Devils cannot fight back to beat Villa, though, they will enter the international break in 19th place in the Premier League table after Sunderland's surprise 1-0 win over Chelsea lifted the Black Cats off the bottom.

Even if Man United fell to a catastrophic loss vs. Roma in midweek, Carrick would have almost certainly taken the reins against Aston Villa, as the hierarchy always intended to get to the international break before conducting a thorough review.

The former Red Devils midfielder is still widely adored by the majority of the fanbase, whose frustrations are instead directed towards the Glazers, INEOS and the players themselves.

Man United cannot correct years of terrible transfer calls and a toxic culture overnight, but they can make a coaching change in the blink of an eye, and Carrick would undoubtedly be the fall guy if the powers-that-be decide that change if necessary.

Fernandes publicly calling out the tactics of the coaching staff hinted at discontent behind the scenes, and unless Man United pull off another fabulous fightback on Sunday, Carrick will surely be taking charge of his beloved club for the final time.

Stockport County will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Tranmere Rovers to Edgeley Park on Tuesday in the EFL Trophy.

The hosts have already secured their place in the knockout stages, while the visitors could join them with a win.

Stockport currently sit second in League One with 26 points from their opening 14 matches and are among the favourites to earn promotion to the Championship this season.

Jimmy McNulty's side beat Wimbledon 2-1 in their most recent league game, with Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis scoring in the second half as Stockport came from behind to earn an important win.

The Hatters have also enjoyed an excellent EFL Trophy campaign, recording a 6-3 victory over Everton Under-21s before beating Shrewsbury Town 2-0 to secure their spot in the knockouts.

It is also worth noting that Stockport have only lost to Tranmere twice since 2010, including beating them 3-1 in their most recent meeting in the FA Cup last season.

Tranmere, meanwhile, are 11th in League Two with 19 points from 14 matches and they travel to Greater Manchester following a disappointing FA Cup exit on Saturday.

Darrell Clarke's side were beaten 3-0 by Barnet, with Kane Smith, Nnamdi Oforbh and Damola Ajayi all scoring in the final stages of the game.

However, the Rovers are unbeaten in their last three league games, having picked up a 3-1 win over Cheltenham Town in their most recent fixture.

In the EFL Trophy, Tranmere have only played one game so far, which saw them beat Shrewsbury Town 1-0 thanks to a Dylan Jones strike.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Luca Ashby-Hammond has been Stockport's EFL Trophy goalkeeper, but he was sent off against Cray Wanderers on Saturday and Oliver Whatmuff is expected to start instead.

Mickael Mandron is likely to start up front, with top scorer Kyle Wootton rested, while Oliver Norwood and Lewis Fiorini are set to continue in midfield.

Tranmere will be hoping top scorer Dylan Jones can continue his good form after he bagged a brace against Cheltenham.

Will Vaulks and Tom Conlon are expected to continue their midfield partnership, while Tom Ince is set to start in the No.10 role.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Dacres-Cogley, Wilson-Brown, Jobe; Ennis, Norwood, Fiorini, Adigun; Glover, Mandron, Wood

Tranmere Rovers possible starting lineup:

McGee; Senior, Faulkner, Nevett, Slater; Conlon, Vaulks; Jones, Ince, Whitaker; Ironside

Stockport are in better form than Tranmere and should have enough quality to pick up the win even if they decide to rotate.

#1866. When will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and who could replace him as manager?

Michael Carrick’s days as Manchester United manager are numbered, according to reports.

The pressure has been mounting on Carrick following a disappointing start to the season, and the situation took a turn for the worse over the weekend as, without kicking a ball, Man Utd slipped into the Premier League relegation zone after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City.

Man United then fought back from two goals down twice to draw at home with Aston Villa on Sunday, but the result was not enough to climb out of the bottom three.

As previously reported by The Athletic, United hierarchy held talks about Carrick’s future as head coach following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on October 25.

Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked at that point and then again after Man Utd were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea in the Premier League, a result that sent them crashing down the table.

However, it was agreed that Carrick would oversee the Roma and Aston Villa games before his situation would be reassessed prior to the international break.

Now, even though Carrick ended a nine-game run without a victory in thrilling fashion against Roma, the first half performance was a disaster and United could have easily found themselves three or four goals down at half-time.

Of course, the second half did prove that the players are playing for Carrick, so much so that Matheus Cunha went overboard in getting himself sent-off after turning the game on its head with two quickfire goals.

There was the argument that Man Utd picked up some much-needed momentum, but the calamitous fashion of Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa suggested there was nothing of the sort.

It would appear that United going into the international break in the relegation zone has proven to be the final straw for Carrick as the Athletic reported on Monday night that he is expected to be relieved of his duties.

While it remains to be seen when Carrick’s departure is made official, it is understood that a managerial change is expected before Man United face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday (November 22).

As per reports, Manchester United's football operations leadership, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox hold all the power with regards to Carrick’s future.

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 18:18, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:20

Huddersfield Town will look to cement first place in their EFL Trophy clash with visitors Liverpool Under-21s on Tuesday at Accu Stadium.

The Terriers are first with six points in their group and know they will advance into the knockouts, whereas the away side are third with two points and have already been eliminated from the group stage.

Huddersfield are almost certain to claim top spot, as though they are level on points with Doncaster Rovers, they boast a five goal difference advantage with one game left to play, while their rivals' group stage has finished.

In their first two games in the tournament, the Terriers managed to score eight goals, with their latest result in the competition a 5-0 victory against Rochdale on October 6.

Head coach Martin Drury could be forgiven for focusing on League One considering his team are first in the third tier with 29 points from 14 matchweeks and have a strong chance of securing promotion.

The hosts' form of late has been exceptional, as while they lost 2-1 against Exeter City in the FA Cup on Saturday, they had won six and drawn two of their prior eight fixtures.

Huddersfield have failed to claim victory in three of their last five outings at Accu Stadium, though they only suffered one loss in that time.

Liverpool Under-21s know they have finished third in the group given they are four points from second-placed Doncaster Rovers, while they are one point ahead of Rochdale, who have no more fixtures left to play.

The Reds at least come into their next contest on the back of three triumphs from their past five clashes, a period in which they were beaten just once.

Rob Page's side are seventh in the Premier League 2 with 11 points from a possible 18, while they boast a game in hand on five of the teams above them, and a win would see them rise to fourth.

It will concern the head coach that his side have lost three of their six most recent away games, winning just once in that stretch.

In those away contests, Liverpool conceded nine goals and scored six times, and they failed to keep a clean sheet.

Liverpool Under-21s form (all competitions):

Midfielders Ryan Ledson and Ethan Brierley may play behind attacking midfielder David Kasumu, while Samson Tovide is a candidate to lead the line up front.

As for Liverpool, talent Will Wright will hope to be given another chance to impress as the team's striker, though he will need support from Michael Laffey.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa has been ruled out of England’s Nations League match against Croatia, with James Hill called up to the senior squad for the first time.

Konsa will play no part in the first of those matches and he is training away from Thomas Tuchel’s main group as he follows his own programme.

However, the defender has still been fit enough to start each of Arsenal’s last 12 matches across the Premier League and Champions League.

He has been one of the Gunners’ best players this season, slotting in alongside Gabriel in defence and filling the void left by the injured William Saliba.

With Saliba now fit again and closing in on a return to first-team action, Konsa faces a fight to keep his place in Mikel Arteta’s side.

Despite that fitness concern in Prague, Konsa was passed fit to face Hull on Sunday and he played the full 90 minutes.

He appeared to come through that without any further issues, but it has been decided that he should miss the Croatia match with a view to being available for a clash with Spain that could well decide top spot in the Nations League group.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Championship leaders Birmingham City have confirmed NFL legend Tom Brady has left his role as the club's minority owner and advisory board chairman.

Brady was part of a high-profile takeover of the Blues in 2023, partnering with Knighthead Capital Management, led by Tom Wagner.

The seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback was initially a highly visible presence during an eventful time for the club, who were relegated to League One in 2023-24.

The Blues bounced back at the first attempt with a Football League-record haul of 111 points under Chris Davies, who then oversaw a 10th-placed finish in the second tier last term.

Now, with Birmingham sitting top of the table and pushing to return to the Premier League for the first time since 2011, Brady has parted ways with the club.

“In his final season as a manager, we played a great game against United with Southampton. In the press conference after, he said we’d been the most complete opponent that United had faced.

“Through the secretary of the League Managers Association, he asked for my phone number so that we could have lunch. It was a meeting in London between colleagues – between a genius and an apprentice.”

Pochettino interviewed for the manager role at Old Trafford in 2018, losing out to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Speculation linked Pochettino to the Man United job again in 2022, with the Argentine then in charge of French giants Paris Saint-Germain.

Pochettino hinted that he would have discussed the possibility in more concrete terms if his situation had allowed.

He explained: “I was under contract at PSG.

“After our Champions League elimination against Real Madrid, we had no option but to make sure we secured the Ligue 1 title at least.

“United were in a hurry to announce their new manager before the end of that season because the situation had become unsustainable. I couldn’t negotiate, whereas Ajax gave Ten Hag the flexibility to do so.”

The former Southampton manager also told L’Equipe earlier this year that he would relish a chance to return to the Premier League.

Contracts and commitments may once again prevent Pochettino from taking the Manchester United job. After leading the USA in their home World Cup, Pochettino signed a new contract in August - presenting a potential stumbling block when it comes to compensation.

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 18:36, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:48

Harry Kane produced another influential performance for Bayern Munich as the Bundesliga champions maintained their position at the top of the table with a 2-1 victory over Mainz on Saturday.

The England captain assisted both goals as Vincent Kompany's side secured an important three points at the MEWA Arena, with Joshua Kimmich and Lennart Karl finding the back of the net.

Harry Kane leading the Bundesliga in assists https://t.co/2iMHUnpU1k

Kane's two assists were particularly significant as they took his tally in the league this season to eight, meaning he has already equalled his best return in a single Bundesliga campaign.

According to Opta, no player has registered more assists during the first nine matchdays of a Bundesliga campaign since they began collecting the data in the 2004-05 season.

Kane is now on course to surpass his best return of 14 assists in a league season, achieved during his final campaign at Tottenham Hotspur in 2020-21, and the German media was full of praise for his performance against Mainz.

Newspaper BILD said he "glänzt diesmal vor allem als Vorbereiter"which means that Kane "shone primarily as a provider".

However, they also noted that "the only thing missing for the Ballon d'Or winner was a goal of his own", with Kane failing to score in his last four games across all competitions for Bayern.

T-online, meanwhile, wrote that Kane "impressed with his excellent vision, ability to switch play, and passing" but that he was "unlucky with his own finishing".

The official Bundesliga website wrote an article titled "Bayern Munich's Harry Kane shows there is more to his game in Mainz win".

The piece stated that Kane's return in front of goal has been "slightly below his admittedly high standards", but stated that he "remains directly involved in Bayern’s success on the pitch" and that it was "no surprise Bayern were eager to offer him a new contract".

Kane will be keen to get back to his best in front of goal, but it is great to see him demonstrating his value in other ways after extending his stay at Bayern until 2029.

The 33-year-old remains one of Europe's most prolific goalscorers, having bagged 10 goals in 15 games across all competitions so far, but his ability to create opportunities for teammates has become an increasingly important part of his game.

#1857. Tavernes vs Valencia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 19:24, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 19:26

Tavernes will experience the biggest night in their history on Tuesday when they face Valencia in a Copa del Rey first-round tie, with the sixth-tier side officially playing at Mestalla despite being the nominal hosts.

Tavernes' own ground did not meet the RFEF's requirements for the fixture, meaning Los Che will technically be the away side at their own stadium, and the match comes at a difficult point in the season for both clubs, albeit for very different reasons.

Valencia are eight-time winners of the Copa del Rey but have not lifted the domestic cup since 2018-19, when they beat Barcelona to claim the silverware.

For the third time since losing the 2021-22 final to Real Betis, Los Blanquinegros reached the quarter-finals last season, although their run ended at that stage following a 2-1 defeat to Athletic Bilbao.

Valencia are hardly approaching Tuesday's tie in convincing form, having managed just two victories from 12 league matches this season (D3, L7), while Javier Aguirre has won only one of his five games since replacing Carlos Corberan in September.

Los Ches head into the encounter on the back of a 3-0 defeat to Real Madrid, a result that left them 19th in the La Liga table with just nine points from their opening 12 fixtures.

Valencia’s main problem this season has been a lack of goals, with their tally of eight the joint-lowest in the division, but facing a side five divisions below them in Tuesday's Copa del Rey encounter should offer some encouragement.

Reaching this stage of the competition represents a major achievement for Tavernes, who secured their first-ever Copa del Rey appearance after winning the fifth edition of La Nostra Copa.

The sixth-tier side beat CD Onda 1-0 in the final of that competition before overcoming UD Maracena in a preliminary-round penalty shootout, having drawn 1-1 away in the first leg before playing out a goalless stalemate in the return fixture.

Tavernes' historic cup achievement has come amid a difficult 2026-27 campaign, with the club managing just two victories in regulation time from 11 competitive matches (D2, L2) and experiencing a change in management in October.

Following the dismissal of Carlos Sapina, Edu Palomares returned to the club for his second spell in charge and has won one and lost the other of his two matches, beating CFI Alicante 3-2 on October 25 before losing 2-0 to Gandia last time out, leaving them 14th in the Lliga Comunitat Sud table.

Tavernes should have enough time to recover after their scheduled weekend fixture against Rayo Ibense was postponed, which could give them a slight advantage over opponents who have had fewer days to prepare for the cup tie.

Valencia are expected to remain without Sergi Canos and Diego Lopez, both of whom are recovering from serious knee injuries, while David Otorbi is dealing with a hamstring problem and Dimitri Foulquier is doubtful with a muscular issue.

Jose Gaya was sent off against Real Madrid but is eligible to feature here, as league red-card suspensions do not carry over into cup competitions.

Head coach Aguirre could make several changes, with the likes of Jesus Vazquez, Filip Ugrinic and Arnau Martinez pushing for starts, while Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott could make his first start for the club.

As for Tavernes, Javier Pelegri is expected to start in goal, with Alex Magraner and Pablo Nadal Peris operating as full-backs and Jordi Melo partnering Artur Hayrapetyan in central defence.

Antonio Santandreu and Sergio Bono could provide the central midfield cover, with Edu Alberola operating in a more advanced role, while Joan Brines offers width and Jorge Seral is likely to partner Joan Talens up front.

Pelegrí; Magraner, Melo, Hayrapetyan, Nadal Peris; Brines, Santandreu, Bono, Alberola; Seral, Joan Talens

Van Oevelen; Martinez, De Haas, Diakhaby, Vazquez; Rioja, Pepelu, Ugrinic, Elliott; Sadiq, Blazquez

Tavernes deserve credit for reaching the first round of the Copa del Rey, but despite Valencia's recent struggles, the gulf in quality between the two sides appears too wide for an upset, and we expect Los Che to secure a comfortable victory.

#1855. Man United's secret plot to poach Sir Alex Ferguson from Aberdeen, 40 years on - from phone calls with a fake Scottish accent to clandestine meetings at M74 services on Bonfire Night

Published: 04:53 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 6 November 2026

It is 40 years ago today since Manchester United appointed Sir Alex Ferguson as manager and ushered in the most successful era in the history of the club.

The parallels with the current situation at Old Trafford are striking. United have made their worst start to a league season since then, with just one win from their opening nine games, and Michael Carrick is fighting to save his job, just as Ron Atkinson was on the brink in November 1986.

United had rejected Big Ron’s offer to resign towards the end of the previous season. However, with the team only staying out of the relegation zone on goal difference, the club decided to sack him following a 4-1 League Cup defeat by Southampton.

Atkinson felt the seeds of a decision that would change the course of United’s history had been sown a few months earlier when he was working as a TV pundit at the World Cup in Mexico and Aberdeen boss Ferguson was in temporary charge of Scotland, following the sudden death of Jock Stein.

‘Lawrie McMenemy, also on the World Cup beat as a TV pundit, revealed he had heard Alex Ferguson had already been tapped up for my job,’ Atkinson later wrote in his autobiography.

‘I haven’t lost any sleep about the shenanigans surrounding my premature departure. I don’t blame Alex one bit. It’s all part of the management game. Somebody is inevitably waiting to nick your boots in this business.’

It is 40 years since Manchester United secretively lured Sir Alex Ferguson from Aberdeen

Club director Mike Edelson put on a fake Scottish accent to get through to Ferguson's office at Aberdeen, posing as Gordon Strachan's assistant

Atkinson’s suspicions were founded on a conversation between Ferguson and United director Sir Bobby Charlton in Mexico. Ferguson confirmed the chat, but disputes its significance.

‘That’s not true,’ Ferguson wrote, addressing Atkinson’s claim in his book Managing My Life. ‘Although Bobby did speak to me at the side of the pitch before Scotland’s fiasco of a game in Uruguay, the furthest he went was to ask that if I ever decided to move to England, I should let him know. I don’t think that could be considered an offer.

‘Apart from the brief contact with Bobby, there was nothing but rumour to link me with Old Trafford before November 5.’

Charlton’s recollection also suggests it was incidental. ‘I was working for the BBC and I went to watch Scotland train,’ he told Daily Mail Sport in 2011. ‘He saw me through the fence and came over to say hello. We only spoke for a minute or so, but I liked him.

‘I also recall going to Aberdeen once, to open a garage of all things. The people there were panicking. “You’re not here to take our manager, are you?” The whole city seemed to be in love with him. I stored that away, too.’

Atkinson viewed Charlton as an adversary in the boardroom. When he returned from Mexico keen to complete the signing of England centre back Terry Butcher from Ipswich, using money earmarked from the £2.3million sale of Mark Hughes to Barcelona, Charlton was the main opponent to the move.

Chairman Martin Edwards pulled the plug citing a lack of funds due, in part, to building a new museum at Old Trafford. ‘We’ll bring the museum up for a corner then!’ Atkinson replied.

Having decided a change of manager was needed, United favoured Ferguson over Terry Venables, but were anxious to make sure the 44-year-old wanted the job having drawn a blank with McMenemy, Bobby Robson and Ron Saunders before appointing Atkinson five years earlier.

Club director Martin Edwards spoke with Fergson and met him with a secret delegation at M74 services in Lanarkshire

Ferguson pictured with Graham Hogg (right) in his first week of training at Man United

Edwards, Charlton and fellow directors Mike Edelson and Maurice Watkins hatched a bold plan to get through to Ferguson’s office at Aberdeen by posing as Gordon Strachan’s accountant.

Edelson, who put on a Scottish accent to make the call, said: ‘It suddenly got very embarrassing when the receptionist started asking me personal questions about how my wife was. The other three were rolling around. But she put me through, Alex answered, I quickly explained who I really was and then put him on to Martin.’

Ferguson recalled taking the call in his office. ‘Martin Edwards gave me his number so I could ring him back and thus be assured of the authenticity of the call. I could scarcely contain myself as I dialled the Manchester number. Would I be interested in the job at Man United? Yes, I told him without hesitation.’

Ferguson immediately told his No 2 Archie Knox, but admitted that when he told his wife Cathy she was ‘devastated’ because the family were happy in Aberdeen.

It was her reluctance to move to London that had previously persuaded him to reject Arsenal and Tottenham but this time the opportunity was too good to refuse.

Ferguson arranged to meet the four-man delegation from United at 7pm that night at Hamilton Services on the M74 in Lanarkshire, where they would recognise each other using their car registrations. ‘It really was a case of flashing headlights,’ said Edelson.

Edwards got into Ferguson’s car and the others followed to the home of Cathy’s sister Bridget in the Bishopbriggs suburb of Glasgow.

Ferguson revealed he was offered a ‘disappointing’ salary that was less than he earned in Scotland and had no transfer budget. United also refused his request to buy the family home to ensure a quick sale, or pay back a £40,000 loan from Aberdeen, but he accepted the job anyway.

Ferguson surrounded by photographers in his first game in charge - they lost 2-0 against Oxford United at the Manor Ground

He became the most successful manager in English football history, winning 13 Premier League titles

United’s directors drove back to Manchester that night and Edwards sacked Atkinson at 10.30am on the morning of November 6. Edwards then caught a 2pm flight to Aberdeen with Watkins, who was also United’s solicitor, to conclude the deal with Aberdeen chairman Dick Donald.

Meanwhile, Atkinson was clearing his desk and saying his goodbyes at United before organising a farewell drinks party at his home in Rochdale which was attended by a number of United stars and went on a lot longer than planned.

‘It turned into an all-night rave with more than a hundred people packed into the house and lasted until 5am,’ Atkinson recalled.

There were a few sore heads when a nervous Ferguson gathered the players together on November 7. He was well aware of the drinking culture at Old Trafford and what he felt was Atkinson’s liberal attitude, based on information fed to him by Strachan, who had left Aberdeen for United two years earlier.

‘He cited all sorts of problems with the team, particularly the drinking and the alleged indifference of Big Ron to its damaging effects,’ Ferguson wrote.

‘The training, Gordon suggested, was a shambles, with nothing done until Ron had a session on his sunbed as a preliminary to joining in a small-sided practice game.’

Clamping down on the boozing was one of the first items on Ferguson’s agenda, but not before he banished bus driver Derek Sutton from sitting on the bench following his first game at Oxford 48 hours after being appointed.

It ended with a 2-0 defeat followed by a goalless draw at Norwich as Ferguson made an inauspicious start to a glittering career spanning 26-and-a-half years. His first game at Old Trafford brought a first win, beating QPR 1-0.

In a new book, Fergie: The Lost Tapes, author Wayne Barton has gone through 400 hours of recordings and unearthed a long-forgotten address by the new manager to United fans that day which has echoes of the farewell speech he made on the pitch in 2013.

‘Hello, Alex Ferguson here. I don’t need to tell you how important this day is to me. This is the greatest experience of my life, to be in front of this platform and this stage.

‘Since I’ve arrived here, I’ve been so aware of the traditions and success of this great club. My job is to make sure that success continues and to make us the greatest club in Britain.

‘The real supporters of Manchester United are the greatest in the world - don’t let anyone forget it.’

England face Croatia in the penultimate game of the Nations League group stage, which will see captain Harry Kane become the most-capped player in Three Lions’ history.

Fresh from winning the Ballon d’Or, captain Kane is set to make England history with his 126th cap to move clear of long-time record-holder Peter Shilton.

Croatia head to Wembley, with their mauling at the hands of the Three Lions’ in Rijeka last month still fresh in the memory.

Thomas Tuchel’s side put seven past their hosts without reply, as Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka bagged braces. There were further goals from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, and Morgan Rogers as England wiped the floor with Croatia.

England are poised to advance to the next stage of the Nations League but currently via a second-placed finish, which would set up a quarter final with a big hitter such as France or Portugal.

Victory for England at Wembley would likely set-up a last-game decider with Spain, the winner of that match topping the group.

England vs Croatia is scheduled for a 7.45pm GMT kick-off on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

TV channel: In the UK, England vs Croatia in the 2026/27 Nations League is being televised live and free to air on ITV, with coverage of the match beginning at 7pm BST on ITV1 ahead of a 7:45pm kick-off.

Live stream: Catch the game live online through the ITVX website and app, which is free with a registration.

Live blog: You can follow all the action with Standard Sport’s live blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from England correspondent Dom Smith.

There should be another landmark reached for Ballon d’Or winner Kane on Thursday, with the England skipper set to overtake Shilton as the most capped player for the Three Lions.

Injuries for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa have led to the late call-ups of Dan Burn and James Hill, with the latter hoping to make his England debut.

Other potential debutants include Fulham's Josh King and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham, younger brother of England star Jude.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sweden manager Graham Potter will work closely with Tottenham when it comes to managing Dejan Kulusevski’s return from injury - pledging to have “a close dialogue” with Spurs.

Potter has managed Sweden’s national side since October 2025, five months after Kulusevski’s devastating kneecap injury.

Kulusevski played for the first time in 526 days with an appearance off the bench against Coventry City last month, so Potter has finally been able to call-up the winger for the first time.

However, Potter is well aware of the ongoing need to manage Kulusevski’s fitness.

Potter is quoted by Swedish outlet Sportsbladet as saying: “We are of course in contact with Tottenham and it is logical that we work closely with them. They have worked with Dejan for so long to get him back to the level he is at now. Therefore, it is reasonable that we have a close dialogue.

“We have a pretty good idea of ​​how we can use him. But the most important thing for us is that he is here.”

Kulusevski has required two separate surgeries on his kneecap to correct an issue first sustained while playing for Spurs at the end of the 2025 season. #1847. PSG coach Luis Enrique defends Ferran Torres after nine games without a goal

By Alexis Pereira | 08 Nov 2026 20:49

Luis Enrique has insisted he is not worried about Ferran Torres after the PSG forward went a nine consecutive game, including international matches, without scoring. Paris Saint-Germain extended their winning run to 11 games with a 1-0 victory over Troyes at the Parc des Princes in Ligue 1 before the international break, but Torres, one of their 2026-27 signings, is going through his first period of instability in the French capital.

Torres started on Saturday and was substituted 70 minutes in after four shots, wasting all of the big chances created. The drought has prompted criticism from supporters and the press. Warren Zaire-Emery, whose dangerous header grazed the post, accepted that PSG ‘need to be more efficient to score goals and extend their leads’.

Asked about his compatriot’s dip in form, the Spanish boss tried to restore the striker’s confidence.

‘At the start of 2026-27, everyone was worried about Mika Godts, not Ferran, and now it is the opposite,’ Luis Enrique told reporters. ‘Do not worry about any PSG player. It is normal for strikers to miss chances. What is fundamental for me is that they keep creating clear chances.’

The 26-year-old, who scored the goal that sealed Spain’s second World Cup title, joined PSG from Barcelona in August for £42.5m. He replaced Goncalo Ramos, who joined AC Milan, and was also a request of the manager, who felt he fitted his philosophy perfectly.

Beyond the versatility to play anywhere in the attack, Torres is active without the ball, pressing opposition build-up and moving through the final third to create space for team-mates.

His start in Paris could hardly have been better, with seven goals in his first six games, even though he came off the bench in half of them. Since returning from Spain’s Nations League duty, however, he appears to have lost confidence in front of goal.

As a result, Torres returned to the bench in important matches, including the 6-0 thrashing of Villarreal on Tuesday, when Senny Mayulu and Maghnes Akliouche started in the absence of the injured Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Torres was also criticised for inconsistency at Barcelona, which helps to explain why his boss has been so vocal in protecting him. Luis Enrique praised the effort Torres makes to get into good positions to shoot, saying it is only a matter of time before he finds the net again.

‘I remember last year, we had games in which we had 20 shots and lost in the end,’ the PSG boss said. ‘There are games in which we are more efficient and others in which we are less, and that is football.’

#1846. Michael Carrick sack news LIVE: Manchester United latest as shock twist emerges

Manchester United have decided to sack Michael Carrick as manager following the chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford. The under-fire boss was given Sunday’s draw, and the visit of Roma earlier in the week, which saw Man Utd overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit to win in the Champions League, but it hasn’t proven enough to keep his job.

Widespread reports overnight claim that a decision has finally been made, with Carrick set to depart and a new manager be appointed - though a decision may be delayed until Wednesday or Thursday as Sir Jim Ratcliffe has summoned club chiefs to Monaco. There also remain plenty of questions regarding who the new man could be. Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann were considered early frontrunners, and Antonio Conte is said to be keen, but it is Mauricio Pochettino who is now the favourite to land the job.

United head into the November international break sitting inside the bottom three amid genuine fears over a potential relegation battle this season, having won just one of their first 10 matches - at home to newly-promoted Ipswich back in August - and collected only eight points with a tough trip to Liverpool to come next. Whoever come in has an almighty task on their hands. Follow the latest on Michael Carrick’s Manchester United future live below!

Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is little closer to being resolved.

Despite widespread reports on Monday night claiming a decision has been made to sack the under-pressure manager, Carrick arrived at the club’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday and oversaw training with a depleted group due to international commitments.

It was expected that Carrick would be sacked on Tuesday, with an official announcement to come soon after, but BBC Sport report that it will be at least another day until their is concrete clarity.

Carrick’s future is set to be discussed at a meeting involving Sir Jim Ratcliffe and senior club executives in Monaco on Wednesday.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox on Monday flew out to Monaco for the pre-planned meeting, during which Carrick’s future will be discussed.

BBC Sport add that Berrada and Wilcox are expected to will recommend on Wednesday to minority owner Ratcliffe and the Glazer family that Carrick be dismissed and a new manager be appointed.

A final decision may then not come until Thursday, with Carrick and the club in limbo until official confirmation. Carrick staying has not yet been ruled out.

The idea of Mauricio Pochettino becoming the next Manchester United manager has piqued the interest of Chelsea and Tottenham supporters.

If Pochettino does takeover at Man United, it will be a case of third time lucky having twice previously interviewed for the manager’s job.

Of course, the Argentina tactician is no stranger to the Premier League after enjoying spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea before moving into international management.

Amid reports of talks with United set to commence, some Spurs and Chelsea fans, on social media, have reacted to the idea of seeing their former boss back in English football.

Mauricio Pochettino is expected to face the media on Friday amid ongoing speculation linking him with the Manchester United job.

Pochettino will be addressing reporters ahead of the United States’ Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti, but he will expect to field questions on Man Utd.

Pochettino and his squad are currently based at US Soccer’s national training centre.

The future of Michael Carrick will be decided once and for all at a meeting tomorrow.

That’s according to BBC Sport, who report that a meeting in Monaco has been scheduled for owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox where, among other topics, Carrick will be discussed.

Berrada and Wilcox are expected to recommend to Ratcliffe and the Glazer family that Carrick be sacked. Ratcliffe gets the final say.

It does mean Carrick may not be sacked until Thursday.

Michael Carrick is currently taking first-team training at Carrington.

As it stands, he is still expected to be sacked and most likely today.

This is not a good look for the decision-makers at Manchester United.

Former Manchester United striker Louis Saha is not surprised that Michael Carrick is set to be sacked.

"It's extremely naive to just expect that the squad they had last year would just come and get the same results, thinking Michael Carrick will work some sort of magic,” he told BettingLounge.

"All summer the plan was just unclear, you can’t expect the same results if the support isn’t there. Maybe the stadium plans are now the priority but if that’s the case then the results will suffer on the pitch.

"Clubs are always judged on results and the club can’t forget that.”

Mauricio Pochettino has long been of interest to Manchester United, having twice previously interviewed for the manager job.

Pochettino continues to enjoy a stellar reputation in the Premier League thanks to his work at Tottenham over five-and-a-half years, during which time he twice came close to winning the Premier League title and took Spurs to a Champions League final.

The Argentine's time with Southampton, previous to Spurs, was also eye-catching, while his one-season spell with Chelsea, which ended two years ago, showed signs of promise before his mutually agreed exit.

So it was Pochettino's success at Spurs which twice previously attracted interest internally at Manchester United.

And as Pochettino emerges as the favourite to become the new Man Utd manager, we look back on the previous times he has been sounded out for the job.

Mauricio Pochettino has now the odds-on favourite to be the next Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has been cut from 25/1 last week, into 5/2 yesterday and is now 4/7 to replace Michael Carrick as manager.

Eddie Howe now the second -favourite at 5/2, having been 15/8 favourite a few days ago.

(33/1 bar, odds via Betfair, subject to change.)

Eddie Howe has reportedly turned down a new job offer as he aims to remain in the running to become new Manchester United manager.

The former Newcastle manager is out of work after leaving St James' Park in the summer, and has been considered a strong contender for the Man Utd job with current incumbent Michael Carrick set to be sacked.

Howe was said to be the pick of director of football James Wilcox to replace Carrick, but now Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly the subject of growing broader support behind the scenes with a decision on who to appoint looms.

Despite facing a new rival for the Old Trafford job, Howe has reportedly turned down the Crystal Palace gig.

Palace are expected to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League. Sage and Carrick are now in an unwanted race to be the first managerial departure of the top-flight campaign.

Michael Carrick has arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground ahead of what is expected to be his final day as Manchester United manager.

The Daily Mail report that Carrick arrived at 7.15am, and Manchester Evening News add that on the schedule today is first-team training with the players who are not on international duty.
