#1845. Leeds have the longest unbeaten home run in the Premier League - from new transfer strategy and napping to choosing 'rough and ready' over 'comfy and nice', this is how they turned Elland Road into a fortress again

Published: 06:59 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 09:23 EST, 6 November 2026

We will know a great deal more about the strength of Tottenham’s revival by mid-afternoon on Saturday. If Roberto De Zerbi’s men can escape one of the toughest venues in English football without too much damage, perhaps he really is on to something.

The Elland Road factor is no myth – Leeds United are currently on the longest unbeaten home run of any Premier League side, dating back eight games to a 1-0 reverse against Sunderland on March 3. Since Daniel Farke took over in 2023, only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have more points per game at home.

Farke's Leeds have won 44 of 69 games at Elland Road, losing only eight and scoring a whopping 141 goals.

After collecting a single point from matches at Sunderland and Bournemouth and failing to score in either, Leeds are desperate to be back in front of their own supporters.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at how one of England’s most evocative stadiums is baring its teeth again.

The last time Leeds were in the top flight, their home form was a huge part in their downfall. From 2021-23, Leeds lost nearly half of their home games (16 of 38) and won only nine.

The Elland Road factor is no myth. Since Daniel Farke became Leeds United boss in 2023, only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have more points per game at home

Farke's Leeds have won 44 of 69 games at Elland Road, losing only eight and scoring a whopping 141 goals. They are unbeaten there this season, and recently thrashed Newcastle 4-1

Farke and the players were able to set it right in the Championship, where Leeds won 35 of 47 in the following two campaigns including the play-off semi-final against Norwich. In the Premier League, it was always going to be a different story but Farke, his players and the supporters have responded to the challenge.

‘Since we’ve come back up, people realise how important the home record is and how we need to drive the team on,’ says Dan Moylan, co-owner of the Square Ball fan channel who has been going to Elland Road since 1982.

‘We know what we need to do to help the team. A lot of players will come to Elland Road and not fancy it. So many stadiums are too comfy and nice. We need it a bit rough and ready to get behind our team.

’Daniel Farke has galvanised the fanbase in a steady way. It’s not been spectacular, more of a steady building of momentum. There has been a lot of jeopardy with Leeds in recent seasons as they’ve gone through the divisions. There was a lot of anxiety in the Championship years but when the nerves were shredded, fans seemed to get behind the team more.’

Elland Road has always provoked strong reactions. Leeds supporters will always be hostile towards Gary Neville but the former Manchester United defender and Sky Sports pundit knows the value of these old-school sporting cathedrals.

‘Elland Road was unbelievable,’ Neville has said. 'There was a real nastiness and hostility to it, but it’s a proper football club with an incredible crowd. You always knew you were in for a brutal afternoon.’

Pep Guardiola saw the other side of the same coin. The 2021-22 campaign had few joys for Leeds, as they stayed up on the final day of the season.

‘Since I arrived, I heard many times about what Elland Road means,’ he said after Manchester City won 4-0 there in April 2022. 'At the end, 4-0 down, fighting to stay in the Premier League and singing, chanting, showing support. I can imagine how the people feel.’

Leeds prioritised top-flight experience after coming up in 2025, signing players such as Dominic Calvert-Lewin (centre) who can handle a rough atmosphere

Calvert-Lewin has scored 12 times at Elland Road since joining in summer 2025

To thrive at Elland Road you need players who can handle it when Leeds are struggling – and this was a significant part of their recruitment plan for the Premier League. Mindful of the failures at Elland Road between 2021 and 2023, Leeds took a different approach to recruitment after returning to the Premier League in 2025.

To make the most of their home, Leeds decided that top-flight experience was needed. In came players like Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Sean Longstaff and James Justin – battle-hardened Premier League footballers who know what it is to play in spicy atmospheres. These were men who would not wilt when Elland Road was at its most exacting.

The groundwork was laid in the Championship. For any home match outside the top flight, Leeds will always be heavy favourites – but this is double-edged. If a match against a low-profile club is still goalless after half an hour, fans start to groan. A couple of misplaced passes later and those groans turn to jeers.

It takes a certain kind of character to override those difficulties and in the second tier Leeds found it, racking up 190 points across the two seasons.

Before home games, Leeds have followed the same routine under Farke. They will meet at a hotel in the city on the morning of the match and travel by coach to Elland Road.

The pre-match meal and final tactical briefings will take place at the hotel and for later kick-offs, players are encouraged to have an afternoon nap. Sleep-deprived players with very young children may opt to stay in the hotel the night before the game. They will arrive at the ground 90 minutes before kick-off.

Elland Road is in the initial phase of a major redevelopment project that is designed to take the capacity from around 37,000 to 53,000. That means players now enter the stadium via a different route and can no longer be greeted by fans on their way in.

The mystique remains, though. Harry Wilson and Jayden Bogle were in the Derby side who won a spectacular play-off semi-final at Elland Road in May 2019. Both regard it as the best atmosphere they had ever played in and it played a part in their decision to join Leeds.

Harry Wilson and Jayden Bogle won a play-off semi-final at Elland Road with Derby in May 2019. Both regard it the best atmosphere they've played in

While stadium improvement is crucial, it is just as important that the essence of Elland Road does not slip away

Leeds lean heavily on their fanbase when recruiting. About 150,000 turned out in Leeds city centre to celebrate promotion 18 months ago and the club show videos of those scenes to transfer targets.

It is all part of the Leeds brand and while stadium improvement is crucial, it is just as important that the essence of Elland Road does not slip away.

‘It depends who can afford to get in,’ adds Moylan. ‘The club need to be careful not to price out supporters and they have to make sure young working-class fans can afford it.

‘I’ve seen the ground pretty raucous and animalistic, going back to the 1990s. Football has changed a lot over the years and the moving of kick-off times doesn’t help but on its day Elland Road now is as good as it’s ever been.’ Tottenham have been warned.

#1843. AC Milan Women 0-3 Inter: Chances squandered and a silly red card

Milan Women failed to replicate the heroics of the men’s team in the Derby della Madonnina, conceding three goals against Inter after a silly red card.

After the odd-goal defeat to Como last night time out, Milan Women were out for revenge this afternoon, and perhaps also a little inspired by the men’s win in the derby last weekend. However, Suzanne Bakker’s side made life very difficult for themselves.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Milan actually had a couple of good opportunities to take the lead and make it a very different game. After just four minutes, the veteran Christy Grimshaw got a good chance in the box, but failed to connect with the cross from the left with her head from close range.

About ten minutes later, Mawa Sesay picked up on a loose ball after a mistake by Inter’s backline. However, she somehow missed the target and didn’t even force the goalkeeper to a save, effectively squandering a 1v1 by rushing the shot.

In the second half, the game remained fairly even but one moment proved costly for Milan. As Benedetta Glionna made her way into the box, the aforementioned Grimshaw made her evening worse with a little kick, resulting in a penalty for the away side (somewhat cheap, but fair).

Haley Bugeja made no mistakes from the spot, firing a great shot straight down the middle to give her side the lead in the 57th minute. Milan then began their pursuit of an equaliser after that but instead of a goal, around five minutes later, Sandra Ogalla was sent off.

The goalkeeper used her hands a little bit too early, touching the ball outside the penalty box, and the referee immediately spotted it. Bakker made use of the VAR challenge, prompting the referee to have a look at the screen, but the decision was upheld. A silly red card indeed.

Deputy goalkeeper Sally Rainey was brought on but just a few minutes later, Inter doubled their lead through Glionna. It was a well-worked move, in fairness, but the defending could have been better at the far post. That was in the 67th minute.

Milan tried to get back into the game but struggled with only ten players. And so, in the 83rd minute, Inter were awarded another penalty. This one was even cheaper than the first, as Angelica Soffia barely touched the player.

Despite another VAR check, the decision was upheld and Bugeja bagged her second of the night. That concluded the night from a goalscoring point of view, and Milan Women suffered their second consecutive defeat.

#1842. White does not regret actions that led to England exile

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Ben White insists fans do not know the full story of the incident that led to him making himself unavailable for England duty, adding he does not regret his actions.

White walked out of Gareth Southgate's squad due to personal reasons at the 2022 World Cup, amid suggestions he had fallen out with a member of the coaching staff.

The Arsenal defender opted out of England duty for the remainder of Southgate's tenure, only returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel in March.

White featured in two pre-World Cup friendlies against Uruguay and Japan – being booed by many England supporters in the former game – before an injury kept him out of the final tournament.

Now 29 and with just six senior caps to his name, White may have sacrificed the best years of his international career, but in an interview with BBC Radio 5 Live, he said the details of that 2022 fall-out will remain private.

"People don't know the full story, because I have never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that," White said. "I think that is probably the best way."

Asked if he would act differently if a similar incident occurred now, White replied: "No, I don't think I would. Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.

"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.

"So, it's something that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and it is time to move on. It's been a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now."

Five Gunners representing  Ben, Ezri, Ebs, Myles and Declan have received England call-ups

White's England return was an eventful one, as he was jeered after coming off the bench against Uruguay. He silenced those boos by scoring his first international goal, then conceded a stoppage-time penalty as the Three Lions were pegged back in a 1-1 draw.

Reflecting on that game, White said: "I was thinking, 'don't stand out, just take it nice and easy'. Then I came on and obviously got booed, then I scored, and then I gave away a penalty.

"So, it was obviously full of emotions that night, but it was a good night."

White is part of Tuchel's latest Three Lions squad, with games against Czechia and Spain to come in the Nations League this week – England only need one point to be assured of a quarter-final place.

#1841. London Stadium to host big boxing events and increase concerts as it seeks to reduce £20m taxpayer bill

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

The London Stadium is set to host large-scale boxing matches and increase concerts as the Greater London Authority seeks to reduce the £20 million yearly bill taxpayers face from its operation.

West Ham United’s ground owners want to challenge Wembley as the capital’s premier location for events in a bid to raise much-needed revenue.

The GLA owns the London Stadium LLP and the football team plays there under an agreement running until 2115.

Taxpayers have shouldered the £19 million yearly bill for the operating loss of the stadium.

When West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season, the £4.6 million annual rent was slashed by £2.5 million under terms set out in the club’s contract, pushing this further cost onto Londoners.

Commercial revenues from the former Olympic stadium have also fallen and the GLA will incur higher stewarding costs because there are 23 home games in the Championship compared with 19 in the Premier League.

Under plans going before Newham council on Monday, the stadium authority is seeking permission to increase annual events from 10 to 24.

Boxing and Soccer Aid will be recategorised under the plans so crowds of 85,000 people can attend, up from current restrictions of 60,000.

Maximum capacity for eight events a year will rise to 85,000, while the others will stay at the current capacity of 80,000.

Consecutive nights for concerts will also increase from three to four, under the proposals.

Last summer, the stadium hosted Take That over three nights and Metallica for two in a bid to boost revenue.

But the extra income only just covered the losses incurred by West Ham’s relegation and rent reduction.

Under the stadium authority’s proposals, capacity for all sports events will increase to 62,500 to match the capacity of West Ham games.

Blackburn inflict Parker's first defeat as West Ham rut continues

Parker reveals team talk that sparked incredible West Ham comeback

West Ham produce stunning three-goal comeback in Parker's first game in charge

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

It is hoped that staging more boxing matches at the ground will be a huge cash raiser.

An upcoming bout between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury at Cardiff’s 80,000-seater Principality Stadium in December is expected to bring in excess of £20 million.

It comes after Mayor Sadiq Khan was urged earlier this year to sell the London Stadium to West Ham.

Labour London Assembly member Bassam Mahfouz urged Lord Khan to consider selling the stadium to the football club as way to avoid losing tens of millions of pounds a year.

He said the current arrangement, where West Ham pay rent to use the stadium as their home ground, had proved “disastrous” for London taxpayers.

Over the summer, Lyn Garner, Chair of London Stadium LLP, warned that “the financial situation remains challenging”.

“In 25/26, we are going to finalise the accounts at around a £19m operating loss,” Ms Garner told a meeting of City Hall’s Economy, Culture and Skills Committee.

“This is not unusual. It's been in this ballpark for some time. We have a few peaks and troughs, depending on how many summer events we have.”

She added that 25/26 had been a “particularly bad year for London Stadium, with only two summer concerts”.

#1840. Chelsea news: Xabi Alonso furious with Blues display in Sunderland defeat

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 21:00

Xabi Alonso has admitted that he was left furious with Chelsea's poor performance in the 1-0 defeat to Sunderland.

The Blues travelled to the Stadium of Light with the opportunity to move to within two points of Manchester City in the Premier League table.

Instead, Chelsea lost to a first-half Enzo Le Fee penalty in a game where they failed to create regular opportunities.

Although Morgan Rogers and Danny Welbeck squandered headed chances, the West Londoners could have no complaints with the outcome in the North-East.

Addressing the media at his post-match press conference, that was an opinion shared by Alonso.

Enzo Le Fee dispatches the penalty as Sunderland take the lead against Chelsea! ?⚪️ https://t.co/cCtYsHVWB9

Alonso agreed with the consensus that Chelsea were too slow with the ball and did not assert enough pressure on their opponents.

The Spaniard told reporters: "It wasn't the best one. I think that we didn't deserve more than probably one point.

"The game was really close. Not much happened, to be honest. Just that action. We had the cross from Morgan, but we didn't produce enough to deserve to win.

"We were in the low block. We missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, creativity on the last third to create more chances. You need to be more consistent. We didn't do good enough."

When asked if Chelsea had been "bullied" by Sunderland, he replied: "No, no, not bullied. I would say that it was a situation that we could have defended better.

"A situation that we could have got better advantages in attack. But the game was really competitive. They were waiting for a chance. They got it after the lead.

"We were trying, but we were not producing much. The first goal was so important.Being behind, we didn't produce enough."

Chelsea head into the November international break sitting in fifth place in the Premier League standings.

However, not only are they six points adrift of second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion, they have lost four of 10 top-flight fixtures.

Furthermore, across a four-game period against Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, Chelsea have scored just one goal from open play.

Like in September, there is a strong argument that the enforced break has come at the right time for Alonso.

#1839. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

We are back under way for the second half.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

However, getting the three points might not be the easiest task as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately, and will certainly use all of the support from their fans at the Marassi tomorrow.

➤ Manager: Daniele De Rossi ➤ Form (all comps): W-L-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Osmajic – 4 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Colombo and El Shaarawy – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: None.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but did make sure to express his respect for the Rossoneri.

#1837. Brahim Diaz benched for 11th Real Madrid game in a row, Morocco worries grow

By Alexis Pereira | 08 Nov 2026 21:37

Brahim Diaz has started on the bench for the 11th consecutive game for Real Madrid in all competitions, and Moroccan supporters are growing concerned by the lack of playing time and by the forward’s apparent passivity about it.

Diaz was a substitute on Saturday against Valencia in La Liga and came on in the 84th minute with the result all but decided, Real Madrid winning 3-0 with the last goal coming in the 75th minute.

Beyond the token minutes, it is the way the 27-year-old is being treated that angers his compatriots. Diaz, who has 34 caps and 15 goals for Morocco, is one of the key figures in the national team, and his apparent acceptance of the situation is what frustrates observers.

The versatile forward has been kept out on the right by Arda Guler or summer signing Yan Diomande, who are six and seven years his junior respectively.

‘Maybe it is time to have a bit of pride and leave this club,’ suggested an insider named Youssef, said to be close to the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF). Despite Diaz’s undeniable talent, he fears the player could struggle with fatigue during a tournament through a lack of match fitness.

The former Manchester City player gives the impression that he puts his club above all other considerations and that nothing compares with wearing the white shirt, which has sometimes led to accusations that he undervalues his national team in comparison with Real Madrid.

Signed from Manchester City in January 2019 and then loaned to AC Milan for three seasons, Diaz returned to Real Madrid permanently in the summer of 2023 with a firm intention to establish himself.

He was already limited to a substitute role under Carlo Ancelotti and Xabi Alonso before the Jose Mourinho era, but he played an active part in the club’s Champions League triumph two years ago as a luxury super-sub.

#1836. Thomas Tuchel tells Cole Palmer he 'misses too many opportunities' to play for England after leaving Chelsea star out of his latest squad

By JAMES DUTTON, DEPUTY SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 06:46 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 09:39 EST, 6 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has warned Cole Palmer he 'misses too many opportunities' to play for England, after leaving him out of his latest squad.

The Chelsea star is a high-profile omission ahead of upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, having withdrawn from duty during the last international break with a minor muscular injury.

England were assured Palmer is 100 per cent fit and ready when they contacted Chelsea this week – with his omission purely down to a selection decision from Tuchel and not to do with any fitness issues.

The German said on Friday: 'I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

'We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress.

'It was a long camp, it was two and a half weeks and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary.

Thomas Tuchel has warned Cole Palmer he misses too many opportunities to play for England

Palmer is a high-profile omission from Tuchel's squad for England's upcoming Nations League games

He withdrew from the last squad, leaving boss Thomas Tuchel questioning his commitment

'That's why the credit goes to them, the trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

'So it's not personal and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.'

Last month Tuchel appeared to question Palmer's desire to represent his country, warning he 'misses way too many camps' as the 24-year-old skipped all four England fixtures in September and October.

Palmer had played a full 90 for Chelsea away at Bournemouth before that break, which he then used to fly abroad to the Caribbean with his girlfriend, Olivia Holder, after withdrawing from England duty.

He was accompanied by a personal rehab coach on that trip, and was provided with an injury-specific training and recovery plan by his club.

Palmer started in Chelsea's first fixture when the Premier League returned at home to Brentford with Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisting they were right to take care of their star player themselves.

It has been described as standard procedure for England to make medical checks on players with clubs. While it does not guarantee a call-up, it indicates how Tuchel has been weighing up offering Palmer another chance as he names his next squad on Friday morning.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso (right) said he had not spoken with Palmer about his England omission

Asked if he had spoken with Palmer about his England omission, Alonso said: 'We have not spoken about that. We have been talking about our game on Sunday. We are very happy with Cole.

'He's enjoying his game, he's connecting very well with the other attackers, he's helping the team. I'm very happy with his quality, his attitude, and his impact.

'We have not talked about that (England). We are focused on Chelsea things, how to do better, how to help him, how he can become more and more influential in the game.

'We speak about Chelsea. We speak about us. We have enough on our plate. My impact area is my control area, and that's what we talk about.

'He needs to focus on his thing. His thing is to play football, to enjoy his game, with us, with Chelsea, to connect with his team-mates.

'I would never tell (a player to withdraw). When a player is fully fit, he is selectable. When he is not fit, we try to give the national team the reasonable information to decide together, because sometimes it's not good for the player.

'For example, Anselmino, he has been called up for Argentina, they asked us, he has been training for the last 10 days better, and for him, it's very important to have his first call-up.'

#1833. Report: ‘Tension is rising’ – Milan unhappy with Toulouse’s treatment of Odogu

Tension is rising between the RedBird-owned clubs AC Milan and Toulouse, according to a report, as David Odogu is yet to play a single minute this season.

In the summer, Milan sent several players out on loan, including a couple that they felt could get more playing elsewhere to then come back even stronger. Zachary Athekame springs to mind amid his great success at Lyon, but it hasn’t been as good for everyone.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Odogu, who left to join Toulouse, is yet to play a single minute for his new club. It’s rather strange as the youngster actually looked quite good in pre-season, while he got some playing time for Milan’s first team last season as well.

According to LesViolets, a website dedicated solely to Toulouse, ‘tension is rising’ between the French club and Milan, who loaned out their player with the expectation of at least semi-consistent playing time. Certainly not zero minutes after ten games.

As a result, Milan are looking for a new destination for Odogu and Toulouse aren’t counting on the German defender for the second half of the season. In other words, a loan move is more or less nailed on to happen in January.

It’s a rather strange situation as Toulouse, in case you didn’t know, is also owned by Gerry Cardinale and RedBird. It does show autonomy, which is good in a sense, but Milan were hoping to do more loan deals with the French side in the future. Perhaps not anymore.

It remains to be seen where Odogu will end up next, but in the summer, Anderlecht and Mainz also expressed an interest.

#1831. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

The final whistle is blown in Chicago and that has well and truly been a game of two halves. At half-time, Liverpool were in complete control with a 2-0 lead. However, four Leeds goals in 25 second-half minutes have given Daniel Farke’s side the victory at Soldier Field. Both sides will now return home to the UK.

Aaronson is booked for a cynical pull on Ramsay.

Koumas should score for Liverpool. He is played in behind and for some strange reason Cairns comes a long way out of his goal. Koumas should lift it over Cairns and into the empty net but gets his chip wrong and the shot goes off target.

Leeds’ second half gets even better and Liverpool’s gets even worse. It is a very similar goal to Calvert-Lewin’s first; Ampadu’s long throw is flicked on and Calvert-Lewin meets it, heading past Mamardashvili. This is very much your game of two halves.

Daniel Farke is making a double change as Gnonto and Lienou come on.

Frimpong kicks the ball out of play and he may have a problem. Is it just cramp or more serious than that? He is going to come off and be replaced by Scanlon.

Leeds have come from 2-0 down to lead 3-2 in Chicago. Aaronson’s cross from the left side of the box should be cleared by Jones but he does not put his foot through it. Instead, that allows Longstaff to slot home past Mamardashvili. Leeds have scored three goals in a quarter of an hour.

Leeds are on level terms. A long throw from Ampadu out on the left is flicked on at the near post and Calvert-Lewin has the easiest of tap-ins at the back post. Liverpool were in cruise control at 2-0 up at the break but not have not been at it since half-time.

Justin is played in behind down the left channel and tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin in the centre of the box but Ndiaye steps in with a crucial interception.

Andoni Iraola is going to make a quadruple change. Elliott, Ramsay, Ndiaye and Tsimikas all come on. Szoboszlai is one of those to head off and hands Jones the armband.

Liverpool were much the better side in the first half but have not really been at the races since the break.

Leeds punish Kerkez’s error and get a goal back. Kerkez gifts the ball away inside his own half and Ampadu picks up not far outside the Liverpool penalty area. He spots the run of Aaronson to his left and slides it into the American, who takes one touch before sliding it underneath Mamardashvili and into the Liverpool net.

Wilson is fouled down Leeds’ right and he will take the free-kick. The Welshman clips it in and picks out Calvert-Lewin, whose header goes well wide of the target.

Calvert-Lewin gets a touch past Ndukwe just inside the Liverpool half and drives towards the Liverpool penalty area. It is difficult to know whether it is a shot or a cross from Calvert-Lewin and the ball goes wide of the far post. Bogle did make a run towards the back post and was hoping Calvert-Lewin would pick him out.

Liverpool negotiate a couple of long throws and a corner from Leeds in quick succession.

After Ndukwe’s pass inside his own half is intercepted, Justin decides to shoot from range but Mamardashvili easily saves.

Liverpool have made a number of changes at the break, with Chiesa, Jones, Gravenberch and Koumas all coming on. It takes an absolute age for Leeds to re-emerge, with Liverpool coming back out from the tunnel nearly ten minutes before Leeds. What on earth is going on in the Leeds dressing room at the break? This is ridiculous from Leeds.

The second half begins more than 20 minutes after the first ended. To be exact, 23 minutes is the gap. Calvert-Lewin is one of a few changes at half-time for Leeds, as is former Liverpool man Wilson. We are back under way in Chicago.

Jeremie 🔗 Flo 😍 pic.twitter.com/kxwhYA845Q

Andoni Iraola said before the game that Florian Wirtz would play 45 minutes in his first game of pre-season so we can expect him and Alexander Isak to come off at half-time.

Stateside Reds enjoying the action 🤩 pic.twitter.com/hfwaLmi8xB

Possession: Liverpool 60%-40% LeedsShots: 5-6Shots on target: 3-2Corners: 1-3

The first half is brought to an end and Liverpool take a 2-0 lead into the break courtesy of goals from Chambers and Wirtz.

Szoboszlai clips a delightful cross from the right all the way to the back post, aiming to pick out the run of Kerkez. A goal-kick is given, with the referee deciding the last touch came off Kerkez, but the Hungarian left-back is not happy with that decision. The replays prove why as the last touch came off Bogle.

There will be four minutes of added time at the end of this first half due to the Gudmundsson injury in particular.

Leeds have been forced into one change in this half and they might be forced into another here. As Wirtz scored, two Leeds players collided, which has resulted in Ampadu staying down and receiving treatment. The Leeds captain though does seem to be ok after receiving some treatment.

It is a lovely team goal from Liverpool to take them 2-0 up around five minutes before half-time. Nyoni’s flat ball out to the right side of the box is volleyed first time back across the box by Frimpong. Wirtz runs onto the ball and, from the penalty spot, slots the ball home past Cairns.

After Nyoni makes an interception inside his own half, Liverpool counter. The ball is shifted out to the left, where Ngumoha drives at Bogle. Ngumoha’s step-over takes him past Bogle inside the Leeds penalty area and he drives the ball across the six-yard box but no-one in a Liverpool shirt is on hand to tap it in. Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#1830. Yamal ahead of Messi, Ronaldo at same age, claims Gerrard

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Lamine Yamal is already a level up from where Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were at the same age as the Barcelona superstar.

That is according to Liverpool great Steven Gerrard, who thinks Yamal is already proving himself as a calibre above his peers, too.

Yamal has been a phenomenon since he broke into Barca's first team in 2023.

At the age of 19 years and 120 days, Yamal has already played 167 games for Barca, scoring 62 goals and laying on 57 assists. He has made 37 appearances for Spain, registering 23 goal involvements for La Roja, and playing a key role in their Euro 2024 and World Cup 2026 triumphs.

Since Yamal made his Barca debut at the age of 15 in April 2023, only Harry Kane (204), Kylian Mbappe (179), Erling Haaland (148), Raphinha (130), Mohamed Salah (129) and Michael Olise (125) have registered more goal involvements than Yamal's 119 across all competitions, among players to feature for a team in Europe's top five leagues in that time.

And Gerrard feels Yamal is well ahead of the curve even when compared to the iconic Messi and Ronaldo.

"He's the one player I would say who potentially has that level [of Messi and Ronaldo] if he continues to evolve," Gerrard said on The Overlap Daily.

"Mbappe and Haaland are around there, in terms of being in their prime years right now, but it seems to me that Lamine is just a bit above that.

Congratulations on making the FIFPRO World XI 2026, Lamine! https://t.co/VGjThLhvDB

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 9, 2026

"The biggest challenge for him – and those around him at Barcelona – is how they keep him hungry?

"In terms of talent and potential, he's doing things on a football pitch that I've never seen a 19-year-old do.

"He's more advanced than Ronaldo was at 19. I played against Messi as a youngster, and he's probably more advanced than he was too."

Messi made his Barca debut at the age of 17 in 2004, while at 19, Ronaldo was playing regularly for Manchester United.

The big question for Gerrard is whether Yamal can match the consistent heights that both Messi and Ronaldo have managed over the years.

"Is he going to have the consistency that they both had?" Gerrard said.

"Can he get the goals they did – and will he evolve into a number nine?"

#1829. BK Hacken Women vs Chelsea Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 08 Nov 2026 22:15, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:39

Chelsea Women will head to Sweden for Tuesday's Women's Champions League clash against BK Hacken Women.

The Blues occupy fourth spot in the league phase, while Hacken head into matchday four in 16th position.

Hacken are competing in the Women's Champions League draw for the first time since 2023-24, when they made it out of the group stage before losing to Paris Saint-Germain in the quarter-finals.

Elena Sadiku's side are competing as the reigning UEFA Women's Europa Cup winners after beating fellow Swedish side Hammarby in last season's final to win the inaugural edition of the competition.

Hacken also beat Hammarby to the 2026 Damallsvenskan title, clinching the silverware with a commanding 4-1 victory earlier this month.

After retaining their league crown, Hacken returned to action with a 1-1 draw against Djurgarden on Friday, extending their unbeaten league run to 18 matches.

They will now turn their focus to the league phase, where they are currently two points adrift of a top-12 spot after taking just one point from their opening three matches.

Hacken are currently the league phase's joint second-lowest scorers with just one goal to their name, although that effort did arrive as a stoppage-time equaliser in their most recent European outing against Paris FC.

Chelsea, meanwhile, are one of four teams yet to lose in the Champions League after collecting seven points from their first three league phase games.

The Blues recorded home victories against Austria Vienna and Roma on either side of a goalless away draw against Lyon, laying the foundation for a serious challenge for a top-four spot.

The 2-0 victory over Roma formed part of a five-game winning run that came to a frustrating end in Saturday's 1-1 draw against Everton in the Women's Super League.

Sandi Baltimore grabbed the opener just shy of the half-hour mark, only for Everton to quickly equalise through a Lucy Bronze own goal.

After failing to find the winner, Chelsea dropped two points behind their title rivals Manchester City, who they will face in a crucial WSL clash on Saturday.

However, first they will travel to Sweden for Tuesday's European fixture, with the visitors searching for a fourth consecutive away win as they look to extend their 14-game unbeaten start to the season.

BK Hacken Women Women's Champions League form:

Chelsea Women Women's Champions League form:

The Swedish champions are unable to call upon Helena Sampaio, Lisa Lowing and Elin Rubensson, while Anna Anvegard is a doubt after missing the recent draw against Djurgarden.

Nesrin Akgun will feature in the matchday squad after recovering from injury to make her first appearance since August as a substitute on Friday.

Sadiku is expected to keep changes to a minimum, although she may decide to recall central midfielder Pernille Sanvig for the European fixture.

Chelsea star Lauren James will not feature before the international break after sustaining a hamstring injury in the 6-0 win over Charlton.

In addition to James, the Blues are also without the services of defender Naomi Girma and forward Mayra Ramirez.

Veerle Buurman, Lexi Potter, Alyssa Thompson, Sjoeke Nusken and Aggie Beever-Jones are among those who could receive a starting spot if Bompastor opts to freshen up her side for the midweek away trip.

BK Hacken Women possible starting lineup:

Falk; Rybrink, Luik, Ostlund; Palmadottir, Sanvig, Matriano, Selerud; Tindell, Omewa, Bodin

Hampton; Bronze, Buchanan, Buurman; Carpenter, Walsh, Potter, Baltimore; Thompson, Nusken, Beever-Jones

While Chelsea may have one eye on their upcoming league clash with Man City, they will still be hungry to claim three points in their quest to secure a UWCL quarter-final spot.

The Blues are the clear favourites on paper, and given Hacken's lack of goals in the main draw, we think the visitors should claim a comfortable win.

#1828. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!

#1827. Bromley vs MK Dons - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 08 Nov 2026 22:43

In search of a first win as Bromley manager, Karl Robinson will lead his side into an EFL Trophy contest against former club MK Dons on Tuesday.

MK Dons sit at the top of the group after two games with their place in the knockout rounds confirmed, while their hosts are unable to progress but will still hope to end a winless run.

Bromley will play their second game under the new management of Karl Robinson on Tuesday as they look to get back to winning ways in the midst of a tough spell.

After a memorable 2025-26 in which they won promotion to League One for the first time in their history, they have struggled early in the new term, sitting bottom of the third tier having earned just nine points from their 13 games and winning just two of those while conceding a league-high 33 goals.

That has come alongside back-to-back EFL Trophy defeats for the Ravens at the hands of Brentford Under-21s and Crawley Town, and they also fell short in the FA Cup at the weekend, dropping out in the first round at the hands of fourth-tier Rotherham United.

Their winless run now stands at nine games, including eight defeats, with popular manager Andy Woodman departing in that time, Byron Webster's caretaker spell unable to end their struggles and Robinson's first game in the dugout ending in that first-round defeat.

Now keen to bounce back from that 2-0 cup loss, despite being unable to advance from their EFL Trophy group, Bromley will hope to use Tuesday's game to get up and running under the new boss and build confidence for upcoming league outings.

They meet a fellow League One team in a different position, having already progressed in this competition while building momentum on all fronts in recent weeks.

MK Dons won promotion to the third tier alongside Bromley last season and endured a slow start, but thanks to an upturn in form they now sit 12 on 18 points from 13 games having only lost three of those.

Paul Warne's side have now won seven of their last nine games in all competitions, beginning with consecutive EFL Trophy victories to top the group as they beat Crawley Town and Brentford Under-21s 4-1 and 7-1 respectively.

They headed into the weekend's FA Cup tie on the back of three straight league wins, across which they scored 11 goals, and got past Swindon Athletic to book their second-round spot with Marvin Ekpiteta and Aaron Collins scoring early.

Now on four consecutive victories and with their place in the next round cemented, MK Dons make the trip on Tuesday with the hopes of keeping building momentum with another victory to end the group stage with a perfect record.

While they are out of the competition, Robinson should field a strong Bromley XI as they look to end a winless run and rebuild confidence.

Ashley Charles remains out injured, but Shamal George was able to return between the sticks against Rotherham, while defender Adam Jackson missed out at the weekend after being forced off in the league game prior.

Richard Taylor may again join Kamarl Grant at the back in Jackson's absence, while Mitch Pinnock and Ethon Archer will compete for spots out wide after Mickel Miller, Jodi Jones and JJ McKiernan supported front man Michael Cheek on Saturday.

MK Dons may take the chance to rotate after a busy and productive run of games, and Warne has a deep and strong squad to utilise and allow rests for key men.

They will likely remain without Ryan Barnett, Kane Wilson and Rushian Hepburn-Murphy due to ongoing injuries.

Star forward Aaron Collins will likely sit out, having scored seven goals in the last three games, as may Alex Gilbey, with the likes of Ben Wiles, Daniel Barlaser, Callum Paterson and Ibrahim Fullah able to come in from the outset.

MacGillivray; Jones, Nelson, Sanders; Silvera, Barlaser, Matete, Wiles, Bramall; Fullah, Paterson

Bromley may come into Tuesday's meeting with more to play for in their bid to improve their fortunes this season, but the visitors have an abundance of quality and momentum on their side, and we fancy them, even with rotations, to come out on top away from home.
